newsitem.title: UK: Castoroil seen easing on possible Brazilian export.
newsitem.headline: Castoroil seen easing on possible Brazilian export.

text.p: Castoroil prices look set to ease in the coming months with the possible return of Brazil to the market as an exporter.
European traders expect the Brazilian crop castorseed crop to double this year with 80,000 tonnes of seed being produced allowing it to become an exporter for the first time in three years.
Some traders said the crop could be as high as 100,000 tonnes, but felt a safer bet would be 80,000 at the moment.
"The main crop does not start coming in until July and a lot can happen between now and then," said one
Traders expect Brazil to have around 10,000 to 15,000 tonnes of castoroil for export from July.
Most of the Brazilian oil is expected to go the U.S. but will still have an effect on the world market.
"The total market is around 200,000 to 210,000 tonnes a year so an extra 10,000 to 15,000 tonnes will have some impact no matter where it goes," said one trader.
India, the world biggest producer, is expected to have around 200,000 to 210,000 tonnes of castoroil to export.
Seed production is estimated by European traders at 650,000 tonnes producing 210,000 tonnes of castoroil.

Local disappearance takes the exportable surplus down to 180,000/190,000 tonnes, but traders said there is a carry over figure of 30,000 tonnes making around 210,000 tonnes of oil available for export.
"As you can see supply and demand are in balance so this extra oil from Brazil will have an impact, said one trader.
China, another major producer, has been an importer for some years but traders said demand from it was now drying up.
Traders said if nothing else the return of Brazil as an exporter would break India's monopoly of the market.
"It's never a good thing when one country has a monopoly a market so this is good news," said one.
